title: Air-fryer potato rosti
subtitle: Grated potato pressed into a rosti and air-fried until golden.
excerpt: Grated potato squeezed of moisture, seasoned, and pressed into discs in the air fryer basket. Cooked until crisp and golden on both sides. Makes four rostis. Serves two.
sourceNotes: Rosti is a Swiss dish of grated potato, traditionally pan-fried in butter. The air fryer version requires less fat and produces a similarly crisp exterior, though a light spray of oil is still essential for browning.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely and freeze individually between sheets of baking paper. Reheat in the air fryer at 180°C for 10 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Grate and squeeze the potato up to 2 hours ahead, keep covered in the fridge.

content.text: A rosti fails if too much moisture stays in the grated potato ,  it steams rather than crisps. Squeeze the grated potato in a clean cloth as firmly as possible, then squeeze again. Floury potato varieties (Maris Piper, King Edward) give a better result than waxy types, which hold more water and fall apart more easily.

items.prepNote: medium floury variety (Maris Piper or King Edward), peeled and coarsely grated (about 500 g)

content.text: Coarsely grate the {{potato}} potatoes and place in a clean tea towel. Gather the cloth and twist to squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Open, toss the potato with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper-ground}} of pepper, then squeeze again. Divide into four portions and press each into a flat disc about 1.5 cm thick.

Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Spray the basket generously with cooking oil. Place the rostis in the basket ,  they can fit snugly but should not overlap. Spray the tops with oil. Cook for 9 minutes, flip carefully with a spatula, spray again, and cook for a further 8-9 minutes until golden and crisp on both sides.

items.symptom: Rosti soft and steamed, not crisp
items.cause: Too much moisture left in the potato.
items.fix: Squeeze the grated potato twice: once after grating, once after salting. Salt draws moisture out so the second squeeze removes more.

items.cause: Rosti moved before the bottom surface has set.
items.fix: Wait the full 9 minutes before flipping. The crust binds the potato together ,  if it sticks to the basket, it isn't ready yet.
Keep each rosti to 1.5 cm thick. Thicker rostis do not cook through in 18 minutes at this temperature.

content.text: Air-fryer rosti works as part of a cooked breakfast alongside eggs and bacon, or as a side to smoked salmon and soured cream. The same method works with a mix of potato and grated sweet potato, or potato with grated parsnip stirred in before shaping.
